name: Downtown Spokane
tagline: The falls, Riverfront Park and the core
description: The centre around the Spokane River as it drops over the falls, with Riverfront Park, the Expo 74 pavilion, the theatres and most of the coworking. It is the only genuinely walkable district in the city and the Centennial Trail runs straight through it.
pros: Waterfall and Riverfront Park in the middle
All the coworking and most of the bars
cons: Some blocks feel rough after dark
Winter inversions trap the air here

name: Kendall Yards
tagline: The new-build strip above the river gorge
description: A redeveloped rail yard on the north bank overlooking the gorge, now the city's newest neighbourhood with apartments, a run of good restaurants along Summit Parkway and a night market in summer. The Centennial Trail runs along its river edge.
bestFor: Anyone wanting new-build housing and the best restaurants
pros: Strong restaurant strip and summer night market
cons: The most expensive rents in Spokane

name: South Hill
tagline: The established residential district above the city
description: The large area rising south of downtown, with Manito Park at its centre, older houses on tree-lined streets and the Perry District's small commercial strip. It is the most desirable part of the city to live in and considerably quieter than the core.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a house and a park nearby
pros: Manito Park and mature tree cover
The best housing stock in the city
Perry District cafes and the farmers market
cons: A car is needed for most errands
The hill is a real climb on a bike

name: Garland District
tagline: The old neon strip north of the centre
description: A short commercial strip in north Spokane built around the 1945 Garland Theater and its neon sign, with a cluster of bars, thrift shops and cafes and a residential grid of modest houses around it. It is affordable and has more character than its size suggests.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting a neighbourhood with its own life
pros: Cheaper than downtown or the South Hill
A real commercial strip with bars and cafes
The Garland Theater and its neon
cons: Ten minutes from downtown by car
Housing stock is older and variable

name: Spokane Valley
tagline: The suburban sprawl east towards Idaho
description: A separate city east along the river towards the Idaho line, low-density and car-dependent, with the cheapest housing in the metro area and the shortest drive to Coeur d'Alene and the lakes. The Centennial Trail runs the whole way through it.
bestFor: Budget stays with a car and weekends in Idaho
pros: The cheapest rents in the metro area
cons: No walkable centre of any kind
Fifteen to twenty minutes from downtown
